items.title: Dave Valentin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: Machito, Donyado Desontes, Tito Rodriguez... So it was a combination of what we call hebajro music... and also the era of the Palladium, which my parents used to go to the Palladium

ctx.x: Can I guess that the music you were hearing at that age was not the typical like rock & roll that was happening?

No. No. It was Latin music, what we called Afro-Cuban rhythms, Montunos, cha cha cha, boleros, the bachanga, the charanga, Cuban music, donzonas, aragon, Tito Puente, Machito, Donyado Desontes, Tito Rodriguez, Lalupe, Celia Cruz and a lot of guitar. Tio Lapanchos, Los Motomores. So it was a combination of what we call hebajro music, which is the guitars, the old guys with the guitars on a mountain in Puerto Rico singing, and also the era of the Palladium, which my parents used to go to the Palladium, which is…
Yeah, that kind of healthy competition.
